thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 Detected sustained error-rate increase and tail-latency spikes for long-sequence chat requests in eu-central-1. Metric: 5xx-rate ~3.6% (baseline 0.2%), p99 latency jumped from 220ms -> 2.4s over last 6m. Auto-alerting oncall.
Alex R: I'm looking at the model worker pool logs now. Provider-B GPUS on eu-central are reporting OOM-ish evictions during KV-cache growth for seq>8k.
Maya C: Noted. Are these mostly from a single customer/route or spread?
Sanjay P: Spread across a handful of high-context routes; bigger correlation with 'conversation-stream-long-context' route. A few enterprise keys are doing multi-turn history dumps.
Iris (oncall): Paging ops_lead for mitigation options. We need to avoid global outage.
ops_lead: I'm awake. Suggestion: immediate soft cap on max-context per-request in eu-central via edge policy + reroute >20k context requests to eu-west-1. That avoids hard fail and keeps customers online.
Alex R: Can we do a gradual failover instead of blunt region cutover? I can push a staged routing policy that routes 25% -> eu-west, then 50% etc.
Maya C: Yes please. Also consider temporary quota throttles on non-critical routes and disable embeddings-warmups to reduce KV pressure.
Sanjay P: I can apply a per-route rate-limit for requests with context_size > 8k in eu-central. Proposed rule: limit to 5 r/s per API key for those large-context requests.
ops_lead: Do it. Post the exact commands you run. Keep canary at 25% traffic shift for first 5m.
Sanjay P: Running routing change now.
Sanjay P: ```
# route policy update
redwoodctl routing set --region eu-central-1 --route conversation-stream-long-context --shift-target eu-west-1 --percent 25 --mode gradual
```
Alex R: Applying per-route rate-limit rule now:
Alex R: ```
redwoodctl policy add-rate-limit --region eu-central-1 --route conversation-stream-long-context --predicate "context_tokens>8000" --limit 5/s --scope api_key
```
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: routing policy accepted; rollout started (25% -> eu-west-1).
deploy-bot: :warning: note: backend pool size unchanged, just routing weights.
Maya C: I also pushed a temporary feature flag to disable the 'extended-history-caching' path for non-enterprise tiers in eu-central. This will shave off KV growth.
Maya C: ```
featurectl disable --region eu-central-1 --flag extended-history-caching --teams non-enterprise
```
ops_lead: Good. Support, prepare an outbound note for affected enterprise customers? We may need to offer traffic migration to Dedicated pools if they need higher SLAs.
support_julia: On it. Drafting a short message to customers who hit 5xx or >3s latency referencing we are mitigating with routing and will follow up.
Alex R: Early telemetry: p95 latency trending down in eu-central for normal requests, but 5xx for >8k contexts still at 1.8%. Canary 25% to eu-west shows eu-west workers handling long-contexts fine.
Iris (oncall): Ops, recommend increasing canary to 50% for next 10m then 75% if stable. Would rather a phased migrate than total cut.
ops_lead: Agreed. @Sanjay go to 50% in 3 minutes if no new errors. Keep rate-limit in place.
Sanjay P: Bumping to 50% now.```
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: routing update 50% -> eu-west-1 completed.
Alex R: Noted that provider B's GPU kernel logs show frequent small allocations thrashing the allocator for long-kv sequences. This is the root cause. Even with routing, we should reduce pressure at source.
Maya C: I'll spin up a mitigation: short-term token-cost heuristic to reject requests over 30k tokens with a friendly 429 and link to guidance. That avoids silent OOMs.
Maya C: ```
ratelimitctl create --region eu-central-1 --predicate "tokens>30000" --response 429 --message "Request exceeds soft token cap. Contact support for dedicated capacity."
```
Sanjay P: Also put in a temporary whitelist for named enterprise keys so they can opt into Dedicated or direct eu-west routing.
ops_lead: Good. Support, make sure opt-in flow is documented and we can do quick Dedicated migration.
support_julia: Will coordinate with SEs. I have a list of 6 customers who touched the failing paths. Messaging in progress.
Alex R: After 50% shift, error rate for eu-central dropped to 0.9% and p99 from 2.4s -> 850ms. Still slightly elevated for >16k contexts.
Iris (oncall): Plan for incremental failover complete: move to 75% after next 10m observation window unless regressions. Ops please prepare rollback playbooks.
ops_lead: Rollback steps: 1) revert routing weights, 2) re-enable feature flags, 3) remove rate-limits — documented in runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gradual-region-shift (reference).
Sanjay P: Moving to 75% now.```
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: routing update 75% -> eu-west-1 completed.
Alex R: Telemetry at 75%: eu-central 5xx ~0.35% (close to baseline), long-context p99 ~420ms. eu-west handling long-context with p99 ~520ms. Looks healthy.
Maya C: I'll keep extended-history-caching disabled until we complete cleanup and confirm allocator fix from provider.
ops_lead: Ops note: we'll leave the rate-limit in place for 6 hours then reassess. Also schedule a deep-dive with infra/research on provider B allocator behavior.
Iris (oncall): Handoff to night oncall in 2 hours. Ops, please bundle current mitigations and reasoning in the incident summary.
ops_lead: Will do. Summary draft incoming in thread after we stabilize. Great job team — gradual shepherding worked as intended. :tada:
support_julia: Sent messages to affected customers with mitigation summary and support contacts. No escalations yet.
Alex R: I'll keep a watch for any relapses and start collecting heap traces for provider B.
incident-bot: Incident marked as mitigated for customer-impacting errors in eu-central-1. Monitoring continues. Severity downgraded to P2.
ops_lead: Closing note: postmortem owners assigned to Alex R and Maya C. They will coordinate with provider engineers. Handoff to night oncall: @iris_oncall.
Iris (oncall): Acknowledged. I'll take it through the night and update if anything changes.
summary: soft cap + staged routing -> eu-west, per-route rate-limit for large-context requests, disabled extended-history-caching for non-enterprise, 429 soft token cap, whitelist to opt into dedicated; phased 25->50->75% migration; P2 mitigated
